summary: Code review PASS for the two-phase (STEP 1 cached render + STEP 2 background fetch) defensive fix in widgetTaskHandler.tsx. All 5 verification points from the review request pass. HTTP smoke test on http://localhost:3000/ returns 200. `rest()` now takes `timeoutMs=8000`, creates an AbortController and passes `signal` to fetch (widgetTaskHandler.tsx:155-174). `widgetTaskHandler` reads `widgetInfo.widgetName` once (line 321), calls `renderFor(widgetName, props, initialCache, ...)` IMMEDIATELY after readSettings/readCache and BEFORE any network fetch (line 332), then — only if `shouldFetch` (isClick || isPeriodic || isAdded, line 326) — awaits `fetchFresh()` inside a try/catch (line 340-349) and re-renders with fresh data when returned. Dispatcher `renderFor` correctly routes 'Agenda' → renderAgenda, 'AgendaWeek' → renderWeek, 'AgendaPlus' → renderPlus (lines 312-316). The react-native-android-widget type definition (register-widget-task-handler.d.ts:22) declares `renderWidget` as a plain function with no 'single-call' restriction, so calling it twice in the same task is supported. REMINDER: a fresh EAS Android native build is REQUIRED for these widget-task-handler changes to take effect on-device; web/Expo-Go preview cannot exercise headless widget tasks.

critical_code_review_comments: Nit: `renderFor` silently no-ops if widgetInfo.widgetName is not one of the 3 expected values. For resilience against future widget-name typos, consider adding an `else` branch logging a warning + setting status (e.g. `setStatus('unknown-widget:' + widgetName)`).

Nit: the STEP 2 try/catch at line 340-349 catches thrown errors, but `fetchFresh()` is already written defensively (never throws — rest() swallows network errors and returns {ok:false}). The try/catch is a correct belt-and-braces measure, no change needed.

The 8s per-request timeout multiplied by 4 parallel REST calls (Promise.all) means worst-case STEP 2 wall-time is still ~8s (not 32s) because they run concurrently — well within Android's ~10-20s headless budget. Good.

The fix is in /app/frontend/src/widgets/widgetTaskHandler.tsx lines 155-174 (rest with timeout) and 318-350 (handler). react-native-android-widget allows multiple renderWidget calls per task. The 3 pre-existing TS2367 warnings on lines 46-47 are from readSettings() literal-type narrowing — unrelated to this fix. rca_of_issue: RCA (confirmed by code review): previous handler blocked `renderWidget` behind `await fetchFresh()` which issues 4 parallel Supabase REST calls with no timeout. On Android, headless JS tasks have a ~10-20s execution budget (OEM-dependent). If any single endpoint stalled (DNS, slow 3G, Supabase cold start), the task was killed by Android before `renderWidget` ever fired → user tapped REFRESH and nothing visible happened. Mitigation applied: (1) two-phase render — STEP 1 renders cached state synchronously before any `await`, guaranteeing the widget always updates visually on tap; (2) STEP 2 fetch has an 8s AbortController per REST call so a single hung endpoint cannot stall the whole refresh; (3) STEP 2 re-renders with fresh data when complete, otherwise user still sees correct STEP 1 state. User requires a fresh EAS Android build to receive these changes on-device.
